legacy_tip: ssh is no longer recommended. Install the node service on that computer, add it again with "Computer connects" or "Hub connects", and delete this entry once it's online.
title: Computers
subtitle: Computers connected to the hub. One hub is all you need: install the node service on your other computers, then add them here.
list_footer: Adding takes effect right away; deleting is written to hub.json and applies after the hub restarts. When a computer has several paths, only one is used at a time: local first, then direct, then via a member hub. If it drops, the next one takes over immediately.
empty_body: Pick a way to add one above: "Computer connects" for laptops, "Hub connects" for servers.
way_link_fit: Laptops and computers that change networks
way_link_desc: Persona Link on that computer connects to the hub, so it works behind NAT and after switching networks.
way_service_fit: Servers, dev workstations, and other computers with a fixed address
way_service_desc: The hub connects to the connector on that computer by address, optionally through a SOCKS proxy.
version_mismatch_hint: This computer's node doesn't match the hub's version. Update the node service on that computer
member_only: Configured only on member "{member}"; the primary hub reaches this computer through it. Delete it from that hub's admin page.
pair_link_hint: Create a pairing link for this computer's Persona Link
pair_link_no_tls: Computer connects requires TLS. Turn it on in Network & access first
deleted: Deleted. Restart the hub to apply
id_hint: The identifier the app uses. Can't be changed later
name: Name
name_hint: The name shown in the app. Uses the id if empty
id_invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits, and - _ . only, starting with a letter or digit
add_link_body: Persona Link on that computer connects to this hub. Good for laptops and computers that change networks. Once it's added you get a pairing link right away; paste it on that computer.
link_needs_tls_body: The computer has been added, but the hub has no TLS port yet. Set a TLS listener in Network & access, restart the hub, then create its pairing link from the Computers list.
pair_left: The link works once and expires in {left}.
mac_step1: Install Persona Link (a menu bar app with the node service built in) and open it.
mac_step2: In the menu bar, choose Persona Link › Pair / Change Connection… and paste the link above.
mac_step3: Once the menu shows Connected, it appears online in the list here.
linux_body: After installing Persona Link on that computer (command persona-link, also persona-link on new installs), run this. One command pairs, installs it as a systemd user service, and connects:
linux_linger: To stay connected when nobody is signed in, also run sudo loginctl enable-linger followed by your username.
windows_body: The Windows tray app is still in progress. When it's ready, paste the same link in its tray menu.
pair_link_warning: The link is this computer's credential, so don't post it in group chats. If it expires, regenerate it anytime from the Computers list.
connector_link_invalid: This isn't a connector pairing link (persona://connector?…). Copy the whole link
address_missing: Not in the link; enter it below
address_invalid_example: Use host:port, with IPv6 in brackets, e.g. [2001:db8::30]:18663
paired_connecting: The hub is connecting to it. It shows as online in the list in a few seconds.
add_service_body: The hub connects to the connector on that computer by address. Good for servers, dev workstations, and other computers with a fixed address the hub can reach. First run this on that computer:
add_service_note: Or choose "Let the hub connect" in the Mac menu bar or the Windows tray. It prints a persona://connector?… link that's valid for 10 minutes and works once.
address_required_hint: The link has no address. Enter a host:port the hub can reach
address_optional_hint: Leave empty to use the one in the link. Fill in if the hub should use another address
proxy_hint: Fill in if the hub can only reach it through a SOCKS proxy on some machine
pairing_long: Pairing: the hub is connecting to that computer. This can take up to a minute…
address_invalid: Use host:port, with IPv6 in brackets
repaired_restart: Re-paired. The address changed, so the hub uses it after a restart
repair_body: The connector on this computer no longer recognizes this hub: it was paired with another hub or reinstalled. Run {command} on that computer again (or choose "Let the hub connect" in the menu bar / tray) and paste the new link here.
repair_address_hint: Leave empty to keep the current address. Fill in only if it changed
pairing: Pairing: the hub is connecting to that computer…
rename_hint: Takes effect right away, without a restart or reconnecting. Leave it empty to use the id. The id stays the same.
